subject: SLA: phased uptime exception & monthly credit allocation for pilot
messages:
From: Nick Harris <nick@horizoncloud.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@horizoncloud.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA ask for pilot — uptime floor and monthly remedy treatment

Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — excited to get the pilot going. Our procurement team ran the SLA template and a couple of items came up we wanted to surface before we sign the SOW. High level: the pilot has bursty traffic (onboarding jobs) and we need a temporary exception to the standard uptime floor and to confirm how monthly service credits are allocated for the pilot months.

As a concrete ask: can we agree to a limited 3-month phased exception where HorizonCloud will accept a 99.5% uptime floor (vs your standard 99.9%) for the first 90 days of production cutover, with a modified credit schedule for those months? We want to avoid immediate credit exposure while we tune batching and KV cache.

I attached the SOW for context (Horizon_SOW_v1.pdf). Procurement also asked for a simple mapping of outages to credit dollars — they want to understand worst-case exposure.

Happy to hop on a quick call this week.

—Nick
Nick Harris
Head of Cloud Platform
HorizonCloud
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Nick Harris <nick@horizoncloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask for pilot — uptime floor and monthly remedy treatment

Hi Nick — thanks for the clear ask and the SOW. Looping in Laura (legal) and Ben (account lead) so we can align quickly.

Summary of what we can propose for a 90-day pilot window:
- Pilot uptime floor: 99.5% for the first 90 days after go-live. After 90 days the SLA will revert to standard 99.9% (unless otherwise agreed).
- Credit treatment (phased approach): we suggest a two-part remedy construct so HorizonCloud has visibility but Redwood maintains reasonable exposure: 
  1) Pilot Buffer Credit: a one-time, non-recurring 5% service credit applied to the first monthly invoice following the pilot month where uptime < 99.5%. This is designed to cover tuning gaps.
  2) Escalating Monthly Remedy Pool: for any subsequent pilot month with uptime below thresholds, we allocate monthly credits according to a capped schedule (illustrative below). Credits are drawn from a monthly "remedy pool" that resets each invoice period.
- Illustrative monthly credit schedule (pilot months only):
  - uptime >= 99.5%: 0% credit
  - 99.0% <= uptime < 99.5%: 5% credit (of that month's Redwood charges)
  - 98.0% <= uptime < 99.0%: 12% credit
  - uptime < 98.0%: 25% credit (capped at the monthly remedy pool)
- Monthly remedy pool cap during pilot: 15% of that month's invoice (this is the financial cap on credits each month). The one-time Pilot Buffer Credit is outside the monthly cap and only applies once.

For latency: we propose keeping our standard P95 latency SLO at 450ms for the pilot, but define a separate latency-only credit at 5% if P95 exceeds 600ms for two consecutive invoice periods. This prevents noisy single-day spikes from triggering full uptime credits.

Operational carveouts we recommend (pilot-specific):
- Exclude the first 72 hours after any major migration/cutover event for credit calculation (to allow cache warm-up).
- Standard maintenance windows (we propose weekly 02:00-04:00 UTC maintenance window; outages inside maintenance windows won't count toward credits).

Next steps we need from HorizonCloud:
1) Confirm you can accept the 3-month 99.5% floor and the monthly remedy pool cap of 15% (plus the one-time 5% buffer).
2) Provide a rough estimate of expected monthly token/embedding volume for the pilot months (range is fine).
3) If you have preferred wording for the 72-hour carveout we can draft the clause for the contract.

I've attached a redline template (SLA_Redline_Proposal_20250716.docx) — Laura, Ben: can you review and flag legal wording items or alternative phrasing?

Thanks,
Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Nick Harris <nick@horizoncloud.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jul 2025 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask for pilot — uptime floor and monthly remedy treatment

Sergio / Ben / Nick — I reviewed the proposed construct and have a few legal adjustments and clarifications. Inline/high level:

- Carveouts: the 72-hour warm-up window is acceptable for pilot cutovers but needs to be scoped to "major migration events" with a short notice/approval process (e.g., Redwood must notify HorizonCloud of the migration window 72+ hours in advance unless emergency). We can draft a clause: 
  "Major migration/cutover" means a planned change requiring stateful model cache rehydration where both parties agree on a migration window in writing; the first 72 hours following the agreed migration window are excluded from remedy calculations.

- Pilot Buffer Credit: mark as one-time, non-precedent-setting, and document that acceptance of the buffer does not modify the standard SLA outside the pilot. This prevents it becoming a contractual right for later.

- Remedy Pool cap: we should add a pro-rata mechanism if HorizonCloud disputes the invoice — agreed credits should be applied to the next invoice or, at Redwood's discretion, refunded after remediation confirmation.

- Definition of "uptime" and measurement: clarify that uptime is measured at the public API endpoint level (token-level failures aggregated to service-level), and that scheduled maintenance windows are listed in the Console and excluded.

- Audit / reporting: we will provide a monthly SLA report with sample traces for any outage > 30 minutes. If HorizonCloud requests a deeper audit, we can accommodate at-cost.

I will add these as tracked changes to the docx and upload, but Ben — please keep commercial language concise in client-facing email. Nick — if any of the above is a hard stop, call it out and we can adjust.

-L
Laura Bennett
Head of Contracting, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Nick Harris <nick@horizoncloud.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask for pilot — uptime floor and monthly remedy treatment

Nick — thanks for the quick back-and-forth. Short commercial summary / mutual action plan below so procurement has something to work off: 

Mutual action plan (pilot agreement):
- Week 0: Redwood to send updated SOW + tracked SLA redline (attached: SLA_Redline_Proposal_20250716.docx).
- Go-live (Phase 1): Redwood supports pilot under 99.5% floor for first 90 days. Pilot Buffer Credit = one-time 5% credit on the first impacted invoice (outside monthly cap).
- Monthly credits: remedy pool capped at 15% of monthly invoice; credit schedule as proposed (5%/12%/25% bands).
- Latency: Standard P95 = 450ms. Separate latency credit triggers if P95 > 600ms across two consecutive invoice periods.
- Operational carveouts: first 72 hours post-major-migration + scheduled maintenance windows (Console-published) excluded.
- Reporting: Redwood will publish monthly SLA reports and provide sample traces for outages >30 min.
- Acceptance: Procurement to acknowledge the pilot exception and remedy cap in email. DocuSign will follow for the SOW + SLA amendment.

Nick — can you confirm procurement's acceptance of the remedy cap and the one-time buffer credit? If yes, we'll send the DocuSign package today (I will include the one-line amendment that makes the pilot exceptions timebox: Jul 20, 2025 - Oct 17, 2025).

If procurement prefers an alternate credit cap (e.g., 10% instead of 15%) we can discuss trade-offs (longer pilot grace or reduced buffer).

Thanks — looking forward to getting Phase 1 signed.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference
